method: Use result.text and returned start_index/end_index Unicode-character spans, after separately validating the exact submitted-text SHA-256. Do not apply returned offsets directly to an unnormalized submitted string.
Reconstruct combined AI+assisted fraction as the total length of non-Human Written merged spans divided by total returned-text length; discrepancies below 6e-8 are compatible with float32 rounding.

For each local edit, verify that applying the planned exact old/new replacement to returned baseline text reproduces returned candidate text exactly. Every edited span in this screen lies within a single baseline label.

Compute a same-label counterfactual by giving replacement characters that baseline label and shifting later labels by the replacement length. A zero decoded-label difference means the fraction changed only by character reweighting, including numerator changes when an assisted span itself was shortened.

Use exact matching blocks to identify unchanged text that changed decoded labels. These returned merged spans are not the detector internal inference windows. Score differences do not reveal embeddings or model weights.
A label change in one uncontrolled pair is an observed difference, not proof that the edit caused it. Only the two selected confirmation pairs have new repeated measurements here.

single_word_summary.interpretation: Four small word-edit deltas are entirely character-weight effects with unchanged decoded labels. unchanged_text_relabelled.text: In other developing countries, direct payments made through explicit contracts in exchange for ecosystem services have been proposed as a more cost-effective way to achieve conservation, although further research is needed to assess their impact. To help address this research need, we tested a new model in the Nam Et-Phou Louey National Protected Area (NPA) in Lao PDR, using direct payments to create incentives through ecotourism for villagers to increase wildlife populations. Over four years, we conducted monitoring guided by a theory of change to evaluate assumptions about the links between intermediate results and biological outcomes.
